text:
anya: Proposal: client-initiated stream migration protocol for the edge. idea is a lightweight handshake so a client can move a live streaming request to a different upstream (eg. preemption, pod eviction, autoscale) without losing the conversation context or double-emitting tokens.

sam: high-level ok. what's the latency/CPU cost to do the handoff mid-request?

anya: goal is < 1ms added on path for happy-case handoff. most work is constant-time token exchange and an HMAC check. heavy work only if we need replay.

raj: curious about semantics: do we guarantee exactly-once output? or at-least-once with idempotency helpers?

anya: we aim for at-most-once user-observable emission. implementation plan: upstream keeps a monotonically increasing `emit_seq` per client stream. migrating client provides `last_ack` and a `migration_token` signed by source upstream. new upstream accepts and resumes writing from `emit_seq+1`. if mismatch, fallback to replay from checkpoint.

mike: ordering is tricky across replicas. if new upstream briefly overlaps with old, how do we avoid both sending the same token?

katherine: add a short quiesce window: source stops accepting new user-facing emits once it issues the migration token. it flushes in-flight internal buffers then returns token. new upstream only begins after verifying token and a `handshake_ts`. window should be configurable per route.

anya: rough handshake example:

```\n# client -> new-edge\n{ "type": "migrate_request", "orig_upstream": "edge-a-12", "client_stream_id": "c-42", "last_ack": 1234, "migration_token": "base64sig", "checkpoint_cursor": "ckp-v2" }\n\n# new-edge -> orig-upstream (direct control channel or control plane)\n{ "type": "verify_token", "migration_token": "base64sig" }\n\n# orig-upstream -> new-edge\n{ "type": "token_ok", "emit_seq": 1234, "pending_buffer_hash": "sha256:...", "handoff_deadline": 1670000000 }\n\n# new-edge -> client\n{ "type": "migrate_ack", "start_seq": 1235 }\n```\n
anya: important: token carries HMAC and `orig_upstream` identity so new-edge can call back to verify over mTLS. control plane should be optional but preferred.

sam: if client can't talk to new-edge directly (network lim), can source upstream broker the handshake?

raj: brokered mode is supported: client sends `migrate_request` to source, source opens ephemeral control channel to candidate and returns token when ready. more latency but works for constrained clients.

mike: what about KV cache (prefix/kvcache) transfer? we cannot stream whole KV by default for privacy/perf. we should move an opaque cursor that new-upstream can use to pull allowed prefixes, gated by policy and auth.

anya: agreed. `checkpoint_cursor` is opaque; new-upstream can request specific keys in a controlled RPC. default policy is only request keys needed for immediate continuation; no bulk export.

katherine: flow-control: migration must preserve client backpressure. new-edge needs to wire up the client's transport-level window. suggest we carry a `client_window` metric in handshake and a `start_ack` to avoid overwhelming.

mike: edge case: if new-edge verifies token but then crashes before sending `migrate_ack`, client waits. need timeout and automatic fallback to original path.

anya: agreed. client should keep a local `migration_deadline` and fall back to reusing original connection or retry migration after backoff. server tokens expire quickly to avoid stale acceptance.

sam: security: ensure token replay can't be used to hijack other streams. HMAC + orig_upstream + client_stream_id and short TTL should help. also require mTLS between edges when verifying.

raj: testing: we need a chaos harness that injects preemption, delayed control-plane, and midpackets dropped. I'll add tests that assert no duplicate emits and acceptable tail-latency.

katherine: I'll own a small reference implementation in the edge-proxy repo and a unit test harness. can pair with raj for chaos scenarios.

anya: thanks. owners: @katherine (proto + tests), @raj (chaos + correctness proofs), @mike (ordering model + perf). I'll follow up with a short RFC doc.

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled to `edge-proxy/migration-proto` next Tues. :rocket:

infra-bot: FYI presign key rotation needed for migration tokens; tracking ticket infra#4129.

sam: +1 on proto. want a quick perf bench before canary.

mike: I'll run perf bench on nginx-like worst-case and report numbers.

anya: excellent. small follow-ups: add metrics for `migration_attempt`, `migration_success`, `migration_fallback_reason`. also tag traces with `migration_id`.

katherine: noted. will add metrics/tracing hooks.

mike: sounds good. :+1:

anya: closing thread for now — will post RFC link when ready. :wave:
